title: Maruti Suzuki Fronx Becomes Fastest Indian SUV to Cross 2 Lakh Exports
excerpt: The compact SUV reached the export milestone in under 38 months, cementing Maruti Suzuki's dominance in India's passenger vehicle export market.
body:
• The Maruti Suzuki Fronx has crossed 2 lakh export units in under 38 months, making it the fastest Indian SUV to reach this milestone.
  • Maruti Suzuki's passenger vehicle export share hit 55% in Q1 FY27, with the Fronx as the top exported model for the second consecutive year.
  • The Fronx was India's number one exported passenger vehicle in FY26 with 90,186 units shipped to nearly 100 countries including Japan, South Africa, and Saudi Arabia.
  • Domestically, the Fronx has crossed 5 lakh cumulative sales and is the bestselling Nexa model in FY27 so far.

A Record-Setting Export Run

Maruti Suzuki's Fronx compact SUV has crossed the 2 lakh export mark in under 38 months since its launch, becoming the fastest Indian-made SUV to achieve this milestone. The company confirmed the achievement as its passenger vehicle export market share climbed to 55% in the first quarter of FY27.

The Fronx, manufactured exclusively at Maruti Suzuki's Gujarat facility, began exports in mid-2023 to markets across Latin America, the Middle East, and Africa. It reached 1 lakh exports in just 25 months — itself a record — and has doubled that figure in the 13 months since.

In FY26, the Fronx was India's top exported passenger vehicle with 90,186 units shipped, accounting for 20% of Maruti Suzuki's record exports of 4,43,825 passenger vehicles and roughly 10% of India's total passenger vehicle exports of 9,05,200 units.

Global Footprint Expanding

Maruti Suzuki currently exports 17 models to nearly 100 countries. The Fronx's international appeal received a significant boost when parent company Suzuki Motor Corporation launched it in Japan — making it the first made-in-India SUV from Maruti Suzuki to be sold in the Japanese market. South Africa, Japan, and Saudi Arabia are among the top export destinations.

"Maruti Suzuki's capability to manufacture world-class vehicles for global markets exemplifies the true essence of 'Make in India' initiative."

— Hisashi Takeuchi, Managing Director & CEO, Maruti Suzuki India Limited

The company has been India's top passenger vehicle exporter for four consecutive financial years. In FY25, export volumes exceeded 3.3 lakh units, the highest in any single fiscal year, representing a 17.5% increase over the previous year. The Fronx, Jimny, Baleno, Swift, and Dzire were the leading export models.

Domestic Sales Tell a Parallel Story

The Fronx's export success mirrors its dominance at home. The compact SUV recently became the first Nexa-channel SUV to cross 5 lakh cumulative domestic sales — reaching 5,12,829 units from launch through May 2026, according to Autocar India.

FY26 was the Fronx's best year domestically, with 1,72,363 units sold. In the first two months of FY27, the Fronx has pulled ahead as the bestselling Nexa model with 39,515 units dispatched — a 42% year-on-year increase — giving it a 25% share of Maruti Suzuki's utility vehicle dispatches.

The compact SUV outsold Maruti's larger Grand Vitara by over 88,000 units in FY26 and continues to widen that gap.

What's Driving Demand

The Fronx competes in the sub-4-meter SUV segment against the Tata Punch, Hyundai Exter, and the Toyota Urban Cruiser Taisor — the latter being a rebadged version of the Fronx produced by Maruti for Toyota. Its coupe-SUV styling, turbocharged 1.0-liter Boosterjet engine option, and competitive pricing starting at Rs 6.85 lakh have proven a strong combination across both domestic and international markets.

NCR, Delhi, Mumbai, Kochi, and Bengaluru remain the top domestic markets, with significant traction in Tier 2 cities as well.

Looking Ahead

Maruti Suzuki's export trajectory positions India as an increasingly important manufacturing hub for global passenger vehicles. With the Fronx leading volumes and the company's Q1 FY27 export share at an all-time high of 55%, the momentum shows no signs of slowing. Reports suggest a strong hybrid version of the Fronx is also in development, which could further expand its appeal in markets with stricter emission norms.
